newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda inflation rises to 10 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Uganda inflation rises to 10 pct in April.

text.p: Uganda's annualised headline inflation rose to 10 percent in April from 7.0 percent in March, the central Bank of Uganda said on Wednesday.
The bank blamed the rise on a sharp increase in the prices of staple foods due to a drought that ravaged the growing eastern and northeastern districts earlier in the year.
That drought ended late in March.
The bank also cited rises in the prices of housing, fuel and personal goods for the rise in the inflation rate.
The bank said that the underlying inflation rate rose to 2.6 percent from 1.3 percent during the same period. It added that interest rates generally rose on a tight monetary stance.

Interest rates for 91-, 180- 273- and 364-day T-bills were posted at 11.54 percent, 13.15 percent, 13.86 percent and 14.24 percent respectively in April compared to 9.86 percent, 13.14 percent, 13.65 percent and 13.76 percent respectively in March.
